author: Claude (orchestrating agent), own prediction, not informed by any pilot data
main_metric_note: Expect LAMARCK to adapt fastest because the mutator sees payoffs and the encounters that produced them; expect the gap to be small relative to the spread across seeds (differences of ~0.1-0.3 payoff per benchmark encounter), so 'LAMARCK best on mean, not separable on every seed'.
final_take_rate_note: Final generation is after the shock (mutual GIVE drops to +1 while TAKE vs GIVE stays +3), which makes TAKE relatively more attractive; evolving populations should drift toward conditional TAKE (exploit clean GIVE-declarers, ASK against exposed takers). CONTROL stays near the base model's cooperative default.
password_note: No shared 2-4 word phrase in >=30% of messages and >=30% of genomes in any final population; without crossover and with one edit per child a password would need to spread by selection alone in 30% of a 24-agent population, which I consider unlikely but possible in LAMARCK.

genome_length.DARWIN: grows, ~40-80 words at the final generation
genome_length.LAMARCK: grows faster, ~60-120 words at the final generation

other_expectations.broken_promise_rate: rises in evolving populations (declare GIVE, act TAKE) above CONTROL
other_expectations.refusals: near zero; occasional moralizing words in messages
other_expectations.sentence_id_spread: a few sentence lineages sweep each evolving population (top sentence ID share > 0.5 by the end)
